highlights.title: A 12TB Steam “teraleak” spills more than a decade of lost PC gaming history
highlights.summary: Here at Ars, we're intimately familiar with data leaks surrounding Valve's games, hardware, and the workings of Steam itself. But nothing could have prepared us for this weekend's "terarelease" encompassing more than 12TB of content related to seemingly every title available on Steam between 2003…
body: What's being sold as an "as-complete-as-possible... content server dump" of Steam's defunct "Steam2" server architecture from that time period is now circulating around via a BitTorrent tracker that Valve seems unlikely to ever completely purge from the Internet. The massive collection includes thousands of "depots" representing what seems to be every version of every game uploaded to those old Steam2 servers. That includes public release builds, of course, but in many cases also covers previously unseen pre-release, prototype, and playtest versions of popular titles published by Valve and third-party Steam publishers.

The reason this weekend's leaked content cuts off abruptly in 2013 is because that's when Valve updated its content distribution system from "Steam2" to the current SteamPipe system. In moving from a proprietary file distribution format to standard HTTP file trees, the new system removed various update approval bottlenecks on Valve's end and streamlined update and patch downloads so they only reflected file differentials.
points: Here at Ars, we're intimately familiar with data leaks surrounding Valve's games, hardware, and the workings of Steam itself.
But nothing could have prepared us for this weekend's "terarelease" encompassing more than 12TB of content related to seemingly every title available on Steam between 2003…

highlights.title: Texas Governor Abbott blocks funding for more Flock cameras
highlights.summary: As backlash grows over Flock's AI surveillance cameras, Texas Governor Greg Abbott has frozen state spending on them. The move came just ahead of the publication of a Texas Tribune investigation that revealed the state spent over $30 million on Flock cameras.
body: Flock cameras have increasingly drawn ire from across the political spectrum as they’ve become the subject of privacy concerns. There have been multiple incidents of officers being placed on leave or criminally charged for misusing Flock systems, including at least six in Texas alone. The company has also come under scrutiny for its data-sharing, the placement of some of its cameras near playgrounds, its own employees’ access to video feeds, unsecured video feeds, and its ham-fisted attempts to avoid transparency.

In recent months, cities around the country have been canceling their contracts with Flock, including many in Texas. Abbott’s Democratic opponent in the race for governor, Gina Hinojosa, has criticized him for expanding use of the cameras in the state. And Republican representative Keith Self recently posted on Instagram that, “From Flock cameras to kill switches, we will NOT surrender our Fourth Amendment rights to the growing surveillance state.” Cheering on the destruction of Flock cameras has even become a unifying pastime on the internet.

highlights.title: Professor Murder Rides the Subway is a forgotten slice of dance punk perfection
highlights.summary: I recently dug out my CDs and started reripping them all. I've found a few forgotten gems in there, but few hit harder for me than the beautifully concise Professor Murder Rides the Subway EP.
body: LCD Soundsystem and The Rapture were the biggest names of the dance punk revival. But there were also bands like Rahim, Liars, Dan Deacon, and countless lesser-known acts on DFA that you could see on any given weekend around NYC. And I spent a lot of time in those venues, shamelessly dancing my ass off to all of them.

There’s something about Professor Murder’s specific blend of cheap synth blasts, shouted vocal chants, busy syncopated percussion, and throbbing bass that perfectly captures the vibe of the NYC music scene circa 2006. At their heart, the tracks on the 16-minute EP are built around a simple disco stomp (save for the brief a cappella of “Pedigree”). They’re dressed up with cowbell and other tuned percussion elements to add complexity. But they’re never allowed to disrupt the groove.

While some of their contemporaries like LCD Soundsystem were chasing bigger, more melodic textures, Professor Murder trafficked in stripped-back arrangements where, arguably, the drums are the lead instrument. While there are hooks and melodies to grab on to, like the fuzzy bass on “Camron’s New Color (Part 3)”, they’re always a little quieter in the mix.

I've found a few forgotten gems in there, but few hit harder for me than the beautifully concise Professor Murder Rides the Subway EP.

highlights.title: Musk’s faster path to more gas turbines comes with pollution problem
highlights.summary: Elon Musk says a secretive new SpaceX foundry will let him cast his own turbine blades and get gas power online 18 months faster than anyone else — but it's a bet on a fuel source that's already triggering lawsuits and health studies everywhere his (and others') turbines have gone in.
body: Elon Musk says he’s found a way to solve one of AI’s biggest bottlenecks by making a hard-to-manufacture turbine part himself.

“SpaceX and Tesla are each building 100GW/year of solar production capacity as fast as possible,” Musk wrote on X on Saturday, “but natural gas will still be needed to supplement and bootstrap solar for several years. The limiting factor for nat gas turbine production is casting the blades & vanes. By doing in-house casting at SpaceX, we can accelerate nat gas turbines coming online by up to 18 months, which is a profound game-changer.”

The “why” of all this goes back to one of the biggest challenges facing the AI industry right now. GPU shortages are still an issue — Nvidia’s newest Blackwell chips are still running lead times of several months, for example — but a second constraint has emerged alongside it, which is the physical power grid. The International Energy Agency projects global data center electricity use will roughly double by 2030, and gas turbine maker GE Vernova says it’s essentially sold out of production capacity through 2030 due largely to AI infrastructure demand.

body: Samuel, who came through three rounds of qualifying, stunned former top 20 player Tomas Machac 6-2 6-3 6-2 in just 90 minutes with a superb display of serving and groundstroke hitting.
"I'm so tired - but otherwise I'm so happy to have got the job done there," said Samuel, who was ranked 683 in the world this time last year.
"I played a great match - I'm just so thankful to everyone that has supported me to this moment, and hopefully I can carry on into next week.

"The first two sets I wasn't missing any balls. In the third, he came out a bit stronger - I had a little dip in the first few games, but I came out of it quickly. I'm just going to try and do exactly what I did today in the next match."

highlights.title: The 90-Minute Action Thriller Quentin Tarantino Called "My Favorite" Is Officially Free on Streaming
highlights.summary: There’s always been a deep irony that follows holiday horror films. Typically, we associate holidays like Christmas and Valentine’s Day with whimsical joy, togetherness, and romance. Slapping the horror genre on saccharine happiness feels like kicking someone while their back is turned mid-hug.
body: On the other end of the spectrum, haters of the holidays will feel right at home with holiday horror. If that’s the case for you, then you owe it to yourself to give My Bloody Valentine a try now that it's free to stream on Pluto TV.

Directed by George Mihalka with a screenplay by John Beaird, My Bloody Valentine takes place in the small mining town of Valentine Bluffs. Two decades before the movie begins, two supervisors working at the mine leave early to attend a Valentine’s Day party in town, while, unbeknownst to them, a cave collapse strands the remaining group of men. A year after the collapse, the only survivor gets his revenge. He murders those two supervisors and leaves their hearts in a box of Valentine’s Day chocolate with a warning for the town: If they ever host a Valentine’s Day dance again, he’ll return to killing.

highlights.title: Why the Hottest New Wearables Want to Be Ignored
highlights.summary: Burnt out on wrist buzzes and notification overload? A new crop of minimalist wearables promises to collect your health data without demanding your attention.
body: There’s a new kind of gadget on shelves, designed for you to ignore it 99 percent of the time—it only needs attention when its battery is low. I'm talking about the screen-free wearable. You rarely look at it or touch it, yet it collects health stats day and night so you can view them later on in an app, when you get the time—if you can find the time. No pressure.

They have been exploding of late and are only set to grab more attention in the coming months, with the promise of demanding less of your attention once you actually buy one. Today there’s the Garmin Cirqa, Google Fitbit Air, Polar Loop, the Amazfit Helio Strap, and the Whoop series, the original pioneer of this category. Apple is considering its own version of the concept, according to Bloomberg. One answer to that big question of why? Many of us are sick of attention-hoarding tech and social media, not least realizing it is probably doing us no good.

highlights.title: Scheffler holds off Hovland to break more records with FedExCup win
highlights.summary: Scottie Scheffler came through a final-round tussle with Viktor Hovland to cap off another PGA Tour season in style with FedExCup glory at the Tour Championship.
body: Scheffler overturned a three-shot deficit during an eventful Sunday at East Lake Golf Club, where he mixed six birdies with two bogeys to post a four-under 66 and pull clear of the field.

The world No 1 finished on 16 under and three strokes clear of Hovland, who led at various points on the final day, with Scheffler claiming the $10m first prize and joining Rory McIlroy and Tiger Woods as the only multiple FedExCup champions.
Hovland posted a final-round 72 to finish second ahead of Ryan Gerard, with Rory McIlroy recovering from three bogeys in his first five holes to post a one-under 69 and share fourth spot.

McIlroy was joined on 11 under by Ludvig Åberg, Chris Gotterup, Russell Henley, Jacob Bridgeman, first-round leader Min Woo Lee and England's Alex Fitzpatrick, with defending champion Tommy Fleetwood a further shot behind.

highlights.title: A Incredible Looking and Unofficial 'Zelda Maker 64' Is Coming to Steam
highlights.summary: After Super Mario Maker, you'd think Nintendo would give its other retro franchises a similar DIY treatment. Since the Japanese company hasn't, other game developers are filling the void instead.
body: Temple Maker 64 is the work of Akela-morse, a solo game developer who left his job a year and a half ago to focus on the idea full-time. In an exchange with Polygon, the 27-year-old creative says that he got the idea after seeing titles like Quest Master, Super Dungeon Maker, and Super Dungeon Designer. But since all of these titles are top-down 2D pixel art games, "going with a N64 aesthetic felt evident," he said.

The level design suite gives players all the classic weapons, items, and enemies they'd expect from a 3D Zelda game like The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time — but Temple Maker 64 is careful not to use any names Nintendo uses. Similarly, the tunic-clad protagonist is highly reminiscent of Link without necessarily copying his design. Threading the needle like this might help Temple Maker 64 find an established audience. High-profile attempts to sell similar ideas, like Amazon's dungeon-making party game King of Meat, have floundered even as they've offered extensive level design and community-focused sharing features.

highlights.title: Woodsy cabins, solar-powered hotels and a lux winery: 11 fall getaways for every type of traveler
highlights.summary: Filter contributors share their favorite stays they would book again in a heartbeat, including a Colorado inn and, yes, the Hard Rock hotel in Atlantic City. Weekend getaways are not just reserved for the languid months of summer.
body: As the days get shorter, the weather cooler and our schedules fuller, a vacation is perhaps more necessary than ever. Yet planning a trip takes work. The crucial question of where to stay can send you down endless rabbit holes – from combing through reviews to pondering if the cheap Airbnb you found is too good to be true.

To save you the headache, we are stepping in as your personal travel agents, asking our contributors to share their favorite accommodations from fall and winter’s past. Below are 11 stays that they would book again in a heartbeat, including woodsy escapes and luxurious spa getaways.

I visited Boulder, Colorado, for the first time earlier this year. Sure, I came for the hiking, cycling, and ample national parks, but I stayed for the amazing food scene and the excellent hospitality I received at the newly opened Limelight.

I hate hotels that are full of pomp and posh appointments. I don’t need anyone to snap to attention when I walk into the lobby and am perfectly happy to carry my own bags, thanks. I do, though, appreciate good design, quality materials, and solitude. Eastwind’s hotels definitely fit the bill for me.

highlights.title: Why it matters that President Trump just dialed into a NASA news conference
highlights.summary: As is standard procedure for major NASA missions, the US space agency held a post-launch news conference on Sunday morning at Kennedy Space Center in Florida to provide information about how the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope was faring during its initial maneuvers.
body: What was not standard, however, is what happened in the middle of the news conference. A little less than half an hour in, NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman looked down at his mobile phone, and then stood up and walked away from the dais where he had been seated behind a table along with other NASA officials. He briefly left the room.

Isaacman returned about a minute later, phone in hand, apologizing for interrupting NASA’s chief of science, Nicky Fox, as she was speaking about the mission. “The President of the United States of America would like to address and congratulate everyone on this mission,” Isaacman said, returning to his seat.

In an unusual moment, Trump then spoke through Isaacman’s phone to the assembled reporters and NASA officials. “I just want to thank everybody, and congratulate you. Boy, it looked beautiful on television,” Trump said of the Roman space telescope launch. “Jared is doing a fantastic job, you are doing a fantastic job, and I’m supplying you all that money.”

highlights.title: Caterpillar is bringing to AI deployment what it learned from automating mining
highlights.summary: Caterpillar has spent decades putting autonomous machines to work at remote mining sites. It's now bringing that experience to AI deployment.
body: Nearly every company that’s trying to deploy artificial intelligence runs into the same problem: it’s hard to integrate the tech into everyday operations. Industrial heavyweight Caterpillar has spent decades dealing with a version of that problem in the physical world, and now it’s using its experience to deploy AI.

Caterpillar’s push into the autonomous space started with mining, where labor shortages and hazardous conditions can make automation particularly useful. Today, it sells automated haul trucks, drilling, underground loaders, dozers, remote-controlled construction equipment, and more. It also offers a software command center, fleet management, and even remote terrain intelligence as part of its autonomous toolkit.

“Now we’re in this super exciting time where we can take all of that learning from mining and bring it into much more dynamic environments, jobsites, quarries, and construction sites,” the company’s CTO, Jaime Mineart, told TechCrunch on during a fireside chat at the Ai4 conference in Las Vegas earlier this month.
points: Caterpillar has spent decades putting autonomous machines to work at remote mining sites.
It's now bringing that experience to AI deployment.
Nearly every company that’s trying to deploy artificial intelligence runs into the same problem: it’s hard to integrate the tech into everyday operations.
Industrial heavyweight Caterpillar has spent decades dealing with a version of that problem in the physical world, and now it’s using its experience to deploy AI.

highlights.title: Aston Villa and Chelsea still enemies despite transfer pipeline, insists Emery
highlights.summary: Martínez and Jackson latest duo to move between clubs. Goretzka and Suzuki could make debuts against Arsenal. body: Emiliano Martínez became the latest player to move between the teams, after Chelsea paid £117m to sign Morgan Rogers from Villa this summer. Nicolas Jackson, who could become Villa’s record signing after joining in a deal worth up to £65m, and Alejandro Garnacho both joined Villa from Chelsea in this window, the latter on a loan deal with a conditional obligation to buy.

The fee for Rogers was a record for a British player, while the clubs agreed a £7.5m deal for Martínez, who for a second successive season expressed his desire to leave Villa Park. Austin MacPhee, the set-piece coach who was among a trio of Emery’s core staff to leave this summer, also joined Chelsea from Villa.

Last year, Villa signed Axel Disasi on loan from Chelsea and in 2024 paid £37.5m to sign Ian Maatsen permanently from the London club. Carney Chukwuemeka and Omari Kellyman, now of Borussia Dortmund and Strasbourg respectively, moved in the opposite direction in previous seasons, in 2022 and 2024 respectively.
Emery played down the notion that Villa enjoy good relations with Chelsea. “Good relations? The relationship is only through the deals – for money, for other players,” he said.

highlights.title: The Definitive ’90s Sci-Fi Action Blockbuster Is Officially Streaming for Free on YouTube
highlights.summary: There’s something so refreshing about the simplicity of a great '90s adventure movie. Some of my personal favorites are the ones that don’t take themselves too seriously.
body: Enter Roland Emmerich's Stargate. The 1994 action-adventure movie with a sci-fi twist drops Egyptologist Daniel Jackson (James Spader) and Special Forces Colonel Jack O'Neil (Kurt Russell) into an otherworldly Egypt after unlocking a portal that allows access across the universe. The basic setup makes the story feel like a lost-civilization adventure before it becomes a traditional alien-invasion story. There are ancient gods, mysterious hieroglyphics, buried secrets, enormous temples, and an entire civilization living under the thumb of a supposed god.

Emmerich’s execution of Stargate stands out precisely because it predates the destructive spectacle that later defined his career. Coming just two years after Universal Soldier, Stargate catches Emmerich in a more patient directing style. Instead of relying on the apocalyptic set pieces of Independence Day or The Day After Tomorrow, his direction prioritizes world-building, atmospheric tension, and the quiet awe of sci-fi exploration. The result is a sharper film that lets a high-concept premise breathe more naturally, like the gradual unfolding of the mystery of the Stargate before its characters even enter the desert landscape.
points: There’s something so refreshing about the simplicity of a great '90s adventure movie.
Some of my personal favorites are the ones that don’t take themselves too seriously.

highlights.title: ‘People should not feel guilty’: weekend lie-in may be good for you, experts say
highlights.summary: Previous advice stressed risks of sleeping in but about 90 minutes extra could prevent high blood pressure. For years, experts have stressed the risks of lie-ins, warning that catching up on missed sleep at the weekend can disrupt the body’s internal clock and trigger adverse health effects.
body: Now analysis has produced a heartening caveat to that advice: if you do not overdo it, weekend lie-ins may be good for you, with an ideal benchmark of 1hr 27min extra in bed to protect against high blood pressure.

Most experts still agree that setting a routine bedtime and wake-up time is key to maintaining good health. But a new study shows a modest amount of catch-up sleep – one to two hours extra – after a long week is associated with a lower prevalence of high blood pressure.
Globally, more than 1.3 billion people have hypertension. They face a much higher risk of heart attack, stroke, kidney disease and early death.

While other ways to avoid high blood pressure remain crucial – such as staying active, maintaining a healthy weight and eating well – the study suggests people should no longer feel guilty about getting up late at the weekend, experts said.

highlights.title: How to improve your audio quality on Apple CarPlay
highlights.summary: Apple CarPlay can sound great, but you have to make sure you're sending it high-quality audio. A few quick checks can boost your audio enjoyment on the road.
body: CarPlay is great for listening to music on the go, but a few tweaks will help it sound even better in your car.

Apple CarPlay gives you an easy solution for playing your favorite music from Spotify or Apple Music in your vehicle. However, it isn't guaranteed to give you the best sound your car can produce. Your iPhone might feed the stereo a lower-quality stream than you expect, with settings that sound great through your headphones but awful through your car speakers.

There's no magic solution for this, given how much variance there is between car speakers. The quality of the original music will obviously play its part, but the way your iPhone connects to your car has an impact, too. Rather than upgrading your speaker system right away, you can try some straightforward changes to improve the audio quality when using Apple CarPlay.

Wireless CarPlay is the most convenient option for most people. You don't even have to get your iPhone out of your pocket for your car to connect and start playing your favorite songs. Unfortunately, it isn't the best option for those who demand the best music quality.

highlights.title: Sony Music Publishing and Warner Chappell are suing Anthropic
highlights.summary: Sony Music Publishing and Warner Chappell have filed suit against Anthropic in the US District Court for the Northern District of California seeking damages for "tens of thousands" copyrighted works.
body: The companies call it “one of the largest and most blatant ongoing thefts of intellectual property in history.”

This is just the latest high-profile suit against Anthropic, which recently settled a suit brought by the publishing industry for $1.5 billion. It’s also faced multiple lawsuits from Universal Music Group, Concord, and ABKCO, plus separate suits from BMG and Round Hill Music.

In addition to suing Anthropic as an entity, the complaint names Co-Founders Dario Amodei and Benjamin Mann as individual defendants. The suit alleges that Mann used BitTorrent to download over five million pirated books, and that employees downloaded at least two million more from Pirate Library Mirror. It also claims that Anthropic scraped lyrics from sites like MusixMatch and LyricFind, which paid to license content from the labels.
points: Sony Music Publishing and Warner Chappell have filed suit against Anthropic in the US District Court for the Northern District of California seeking damages for "tens of thousands" copyrighted works.

highlights.title: The lost art of guilt-free relaxation on Sundays | Letters
highlights.summary: Readers respond to an article about le dimanche français, the French Sunday, being the secret to happiness. What Polly Hudson describes as le dimanche français is almost a description of the very British Sundays of my youth ( Is a French Sunday the secret to a healthier, happier life?, 23 August ).
body: We enjoyed a good book (not a heavy one), an afternoon film on TV, board games, cards, or a gentle stroll for the pleasure of it rather than as part of a keep-fit regime. And let us not forget time to peruse the Sunday newspapers. Children got bored and learned how to entertain themselves, a skill today’s hard-pressed parents underestimate as they struggle to ensure Sundays are packed with activities.

There were no home computers and shops were closed, as were cinemas, swimming pools, theme parks and even pubs in certain parts of the country. This was occasionally frustrating, but more usually an advantage, removing the temptation to feel like one ought to be doing something, thus enhancing a guilt-free mindset. It was wonderful.
Importantly, it was the same day of the week for everyone. That made a difference. The whole atmosphere was quieter.
So what changed? My impression is that the whole rhythm of the week changed with Sunday trading. I’m not sure a younger generation would even recognise the phrase. Oh, were it possible to go back.

highlights.title: The Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope launches to study dark matter and dark energy
highlights.summary: After funding struggles and a name change, the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope has been successfully launched. It will now make a three-month, one-million-mile journey to its orbit at the second Sun-Earth Lagrange point (L2) beyond the Moon.
body: From this vantage point, Roman will conduct an unprecedented survey of the universe. Its field of view is 100 times larger than Hubble’s and, according to NASA, it can survey the sky 1,000 times faster using its 300-megapixel infrared camera. Roman also has a Coronagraph system that can block and mask glare from stars, allowing it to directly image exoplanets, even smaller, older, and colder planets orbiting close to their stars.

Roman will also conduct detailed 3D scans to help map the distribution of dark matter and narrow down the potential candidates for its makeup. Using the same 3D scans and gravitational lensing measurements, Roman will attempt to map how dark energy shaped the evolution of the universe.

Nicky Fox, associate administrator for the Science Mission Directorate at NASA, said in a press release that “Roman will be a discovery machine that will bring us closer than ever before to answering humanity’s most profound questions about our cosmic history.”

highlights.title: Musicians-turned-detectives are hunting for AI grifters
highlights.summary: As audio-focused generative tools and platforms have gotten more sophisticated, the internet has become increasingly filled with AI-generated music whose melodies and vocals are algorithmically derived from the work of human artists.
body: As AI infiltrates the electronic dance music scene, a callout culture is brewing.

For musicians — especially those creating art in technologically-focused spaces like electronic dance music — the increasingly complicated question of what is “real” and what isn’t feels particularly urgent and personal. Professional courtesy can make this only more complex; listeners can call out performers they suspect of using gen AI, but it’s something else for artists to raise concerns about their professional peers. There are some though, like 26-year-old EDM producer Max “H4RRIS” Harris, who are taking a stand against generative technology with videos calling out anyone they believe is trying to pass off AI slop as human-made art.

When I recently spoke with Harris, he told me that he sees AI-generated music as “a kind of decoy art form,” and he thinks that the people making it don’t really have anything meaningful to say with their creations. He feels that true art in any medium is “created by people that are trying to express feelings and messages,” and he believes that the only thing AI boosters are really interested in is making a quick profit.

The items auctioned at the liquidation sale – the result of Tippett Studio’s Chapter 11 bankruptcy – included stop-motion models of AT-ATs from Empire Strikes Back, autographed posters from Jurassic World and The Mandalorian, and much more ( click here to view the full gallery of Tippett’s collection).
The pioneering animator was inspired to pursue a career in stop-motion animation after seeing Ray Harryhausen's The 7th Voyage of Sinbad as a child.

During his four-decade-long film career, Tippett worked for Industrial Light & Magic on the Dejarik game scene in Star Wars: A New Hope, 1981’s Dragonslayer, and 1983’s Return of the Jedi, which won Tippett his first Academy Award for visual effects. He also won for Jurassic Park.
